compare.intro: To tell this unit's points apart, look at the ending: て、〜 joins actions in order, てください asks someone to do something and ないでください asks them not to, てもいいです says it is all right, てはいけません says it is not allowed, なくてもいいです says there is no need, ています is an action going on now or a lasting state, に行きます says what you go to do, and つもりです says what you plan to do.

forms.ja: このへやでテレビを[見|み]て{もいいです}。
forms.en: You may watch TV in this room.

forms.tag: してはだめ · you must not
forms.ja: このへやで[電話|でんわ]をかけ{てはいけません}。
forms.en: You must not make phone calls in this room.

forms.tag: しなくてもいい · you don't have to
forms.ja: このへやには[毎日|まいにち][来|こ]な{くてもいいです}。
forms.en: You don't have to come to this room every day.

check.label: Choose the form
check.q: ^ここにペンがたくさんあります^から、ペンはもって（　　）。
why: This says you may bring a pen. But から gives a reason: there are many pens here already. That is a reason you need not bring one, not a reason you may.
This says you must not bring a pen. Many pens being here is not a reason to ban yours.
There are many pens here, so you do not need to bring one: もって来なくてもいいです.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: テストのとき、^となりの[人|ひと]のこたえ^を（　　）。
why: てもいいです says it is all right to look. In a test, looking at the next person's answers is not all right.
ないでください asks you not to do something: during the test, please don't look at the answers of the person next to you.
なくてもいいです says you do not need to look, as if looking were normally asked of you. The point here is that looking is not allowed.
てください asks you to look at the next person's answers. No test asks that.

drill.label: Choose the words
drill.q: A：お[母|かあ]さんはうちにいますか。B：いいえ。[母|はは]は[今|いま]、[店|みせ]へパンを（　　）^[行|い]って^（　　）。
why: 買いに is right, but 行ってください asks the listener to go. B is telling A where Mom is, so it does not fit 母は.
買う cannot join 行って. Before 行きます, use the ます form without ます plus に: 買いに.
買いに行って says she went to buy bread, and います says that is how things are now: she has gone to the shop, so she is not home.
買います cannot join 行って. Take off ます and add に: 買いに.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: わたしは[今|いま]、[中国|ちゅうごく]にすんでいます。^[来年|らいねん]^、[日本|にほん]に（　　）。
why: すみました is the past. 来年 means next year, so the sentence needs a plan.
つもり follows the dictionary form, すむ, not the ます form すみます.
てください asks someone else to do something. Here わたし is talking about my own plan.
すむ is the dictionary form, and すむつもりです says what I plan to do next year: live in Japan.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: [毎日|まいにち]、うちへかえって、てを（　　）^、ごはんを[食|た]べます^。
why: The te-form joins actions in order: I go home, wash my hands, and eat. The last verb, 食べます, gives the ending for the whole sentence.
The sentence goes on after the blank to 食べます, so the verb here takes the te-form, not the ます ending.
てください asks someone to wash. This sentence tells what I do every day, and it goes on after the blank.
The sentence goes on after the blank to 食べます, so the verb here takes the te-form, not ています.

drill.label: Build the sentence
drill.hint: Which food goes with 食べては, and which drink goes with 飲んでも at the end?
drill.full: このへやでパンを{[食|た]べては}いけませんが[水|みず]を[飲|の]んでもいいです。
drill.explain: パンを goes with 食べては, and 食べては goes with いけません: you must not eat bread. が then turns to what is all right: 水を goes with 飲んでもいいです at the end. "You must not eat bread in this room, but you may drink water."

drill.label: Build the sentence
drill.before: [先生|せんせい]、ちょっと[外|そと]へ
drill.hint: What do you go out to do? Which tile joins the te-form to いいですか?
drill.full: [先生|せんせい]、ちょっと[外|そと]へジュースを[買|か]いに{[行|い]って}もいいですか。
drill.explain: ジュースを goes with 買いに, and 買いに goes with 行って: go out to buy juice. Then 行って + もいいですか asks for permission. "Teacher, may I go out for a moment to buy juice?"

exam.label: Choose the answer
exam.q:
A「この　へやで　コーヒーを　飲んでも　いいですか。」
B「すみません、ここでは（　　）。水は　いいですよ。」
options: 飲まなくても　いいです
飲んでは　いけません
飲んでも　いいです
exam.explain: B starts with すみません and then says water is all right, so coffee is not allowed: 飲んでは　いけません. 飲まなくても　いいです says A does not need to drink it, which does not answer a request for permission. 飲んで　ください asks A to drink it, and 飲んでも　いいです allows it; neither fits すみません and the contrast with 水は　いいですよ.

exam.label: Choose the answer
exam.q:
A「この　かみに　名前も　書きますか。」
B「いいえ、名前は（　　）　いいです。ばんごうだけ　書いて　ください。」
exam.explain: B says いいえ and asks for only the number, so there is no need to write the name: 書かなくても　いいです. 書いても　いいです would allow the name, which does not go with いいえ and ばんごうだけ. 書いては goes with いけません, not いいです. 書きますも is not Japanese: も follows the te-form.

exam.label: Build the sentence
exam.before: 今　へやで　いもうとが
exam.after: こえで　電話を　しないで　ください。
exam.full: 今　へやで　いもうとが　ねて　います　{から}　大きい　こえで　電話を　しないで　ください。
exam.explain: ねて, います, から, 大きい. いもうとが goes with ねて　います: she is sleeping now. から gives that as the reason. 大きい goes right before こえで: please don't talk on the phone in a loud voice.

scene.en: A notice board at a school
scene.intro: Tap each word on the notice board in the school hall.

check.label: How the exam asks it
check.q: _まいにち_　午後　五時に　学校の　ドアを　しめます。
check.explain: まいにち, every day, is written 毎日. 母 (mother) looks like 毎 but is a different kanji, and 目 (eye) looks like 日. 毎月 is a real word, but it means every month and is read まいつき.

skill.ask: Until what time is the library open on Friday?
skill.passage:
学校の　としょしつ
月よう日〜木よう日　午前九時〜午後六時
^金よう日　午前九時〜午後三時^
土よう日・日よう日　休み
毎週　水よう日の　午後四時から　そうじを　します。その　時間は　入らないで　ください。
としょしつで　電話を　しないで　ください。
skill.strategy: Find the line that starts with 金よう日 and read the second time on it.

item.q: 金よう日、としょしつは　何時まで　あいて　いますか。
item.explain: The line 金よう日　午前九時〜午後三時 gives the Friday hours. The library opens at nine and closes at three in the afternoon.
why: Nine in the morning is when the library opens, not when it closes.
Four in the afternoon is when cleaning starts on Wednesdays.
Six in the evening is the closing time from Monday to Thursday, not Friday.
